newsitem.title: QATAR: TENNIS-COURIER BEATS HENMAN IN QATAR OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COURIER BEATS HENMAN IN QATAR OPEN FINAL.

text.p: Jim Courier won the Qatar Open on Sunday, thwarting a brave challenge by Britain's Tim Henman with a 7-5 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 victory in the final.
Victory in two hours and 24 minutes sealed the 20th title of the eighth-seeded American's career. Henman was appearing in his first-ever final on the tour.
The match, played in a bitterly cold wind, started well for the 22-year-old Briton as he broke Courier's serve in the opening game.
But Courier, a former double French and Australian Open champion, broke straight back. Henman then took the American's service in the next game but Courier broke back in the sixth game.
Courier clinched the first set, which lasted for 59 minutes, with his fourth set point when Henman hit a return long.

Henman broke serve again in the first game of the second set but Courier hit back to level at 2-2. Henman's nerve was the stronger in the second set tie-break which he secured 7-5 when Courier hit a return long.
But the American's experience eventually told in the deciding set. He raced into a 4-0 lead as the Briton lost heart and control of his game, committing a series of unforced and sloppy errors.
Courier clinched the $84,000 winner's prize when Henman carelessly netted a return.
The American, a former world number one, now rises to 15th in the world rankings, which should guarantee him a seeded place in this month's Australian Open.
Henman, despite his defeat, goes up to 25th, the highest ranking of his career.
